In mathematics, the '''Rost invariant''' is a [[cohomological invariant]] of an [[Absolutely simple group|absolutely simple]] simply connected [[algebraic group]] ''G'' over a field ''k'', which associates an element of the [[Galois cohomology]] group H<sup>3</sup>(''k'', '''Q'''/'''Z'''(2)) to a [[principal homogeneous space]] for ''G''. Here the coefficient group '''Q'''/'''Z'''(2) is the [[tensor product]] of the group of [[Root of unity|roots of unity]] of an [[algebraic closure]] of ''k'' with itself. [[Markus Rost]]<ref>{{citation |last=Rost |first=Markus |title=A (mod 3) invariant for exceptional Jordan algebras |journal=Comptes Rendus de l'Académie des Sciences, Série I |volume=313 |issue=12 |pages=823–827 |year=1991 |mr=1138557}}</ref> first introduced the invariant for groups of type F<sub>4</sub> and later extended it to more general groups in unpublished work that was summarized by Serre in 1995.<ref>{{citation |last=Serre |first=Jean-Pierre |title=Cohomologie galoisienne: progrès et problèmes |journal=Astérisque |volume=227 |issue=4 |pages=229–257 |year=1995 |url=http://www.numdam.org/item?id=SB_1993-1994__36__229_0 |series=Séminaire Bourbaki Exp. No. 783 |mr=1321649}}</ref>

The Rost invariant is a generalization of the [[Arason invariant]].

==Definition==

Suppose that ''G'' is an absolutely almost simple simply connected algebraic group over a field ''k''. The Rost invariant associates an element ''a''(''P'') of the Galois cohomology group H<sup>3</sup>(''k'','''Q'''/'''Z'''(2)) to a ''G''-torsor ''P''.

The element ''a''(''P'') is constructed as follows. For any [[field extension|extension]] ''K'' of ''k'' there is an [[exact sequence]]
:<math>0\rightarrow H^3(K,\mathbf{Q}/\mathbf{Z}(2)) \rightarrow H^3_{et}(P_K, \mathbf{Q}/\mathbf{Z}(2)) \rightarrow \mathbf{Q}/\mathbf{Z}</math>
where the middle group is the [[étale cohomology]] group and '''Q'''/'''Z''' is the geometric part of the cohomology. Choose a finite extension ''K'' of ''k'' such that ''G'' splits over ''K'' and ''P'' has a rational point over ''K''. Then the exact sequence [[split exact sequence|splits]] canonically as a direct sum so the étale cohomology group contains '''Q'''/'''Z''' canonically. The invariant ''a''(''P'') is the image of the element 1/[''K'':''k''] of '''Q'''/'''Z''' under the trace map from H{{su|b=et|p=3}}(''P''<sub>''K''</sub>,'''Q'''/'''Z'''(2)) to H{{su|b=et|p=3}}(''P'','''Q'''/'''Z'''(2)), which lies in the subgroup H<sup>3</sup>(''k'','''Q'''/'''Z'''(2)).

These invariants ''a''(''P'') are functorial in field extensions ''K'' of ''k''; in other words the fit together to form an element of the [[cyclic group]] Inv<sup>3</sup>(''G'','''Q'''/'''Z'''(2)) of cohomological invariants of the group ''G'', which consists of morphisms of the functor ''K''→H<sup>1</sup>(''K'',''G'') to the functor ''K''→H<sup>3</sup>(''K'','''Q'''/'''Z'''(2)). This element of Inv<sup>3</sup>(''G'','''Q'''/'''Z'''(2)) is a generator of the group and is  called the Rost invariant of ''G''.
